title: Install a hot-swap drive carrier in a 1U server: slide it in to the connector, then cam it home with its handle
instruction: Install the drive carrier in the server's empty drive bay and lock its handle.
context: Replacing a failed drive is the commonest hands-on repair in a data center, and data centers are where the compute for AI is built and kept running. Dell's service manual gives the procedure for a 2.5 in hot-swap carrier: with the release handle open, slide the carrier into the bay until it contacts the backplane, then close the handle to lock the carrier in place. Closing the handle is what seats the drive: its hook swings in behind the bay frame and draws the carrier the last few millimetres onto the backplane's connector. A carrier only pushed in by hand stops against the connector, unconnected, and the handle left open does not hold it. In a rack, the units directly above and below the server leave the hand little room in front of its bays.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. Fixed: a 2-post open-frame 19 in rack section (EIA-310; posts 30 cm tall, their 16 mm flanges either side of the 45 cm opening, their fronts at x 19) standing on the table, centred on y 0. In its first rack unit a 1U unit (43.7 mm tall); in its second a Dell PowerEdge R640 1U rack server with the 8 x 2.5 in drive chassis (43.4 cm wide, 4.28 cm tall), unplugged, its underside 4.45 cm above the table, its front towards the robot: the fronts of the drive cage's frame posts at x 19.0, the chassis's front at x 19.8; in its third a second 1U unit, 1.6 mm above the server, its front flush with the posts. Every unit's ears are on the posts. The server's eight drive bays (7.1 cm wide, 1.8 cm tall, at 7.9 cm pitch) are in two rows of four, the lower row's floors 4.75 cm and the upper row's 6.75 cm above the table; each bay's frame post on its -y side has a lip at the front with a notch behind it for the carrier handle's hook, and a SAS connector on the backplane at the back. Seven bays hold Dell 2.5 in hot-swap drive carriers (black fronts, handles shut); the upper row's second bay from the robot's right (centred on y -3.95) is empty. Loose: a Dell 2.5 in hot-swap drive carrier with a drive in it (7.0 x 1.5 x 10.6 cm, black plastic front and handle, steel rails, about 170 g), lying flat on the table in front of the rack with the middle of its front face at x 7.5, y -13, front towards the robot; its handle (6.2 cm long) open, hinged at its front's -y corner and pointing at the robot.
scoring: Checked at the end, measured on the carrier against its home position in the empty bay (its front 1 mm behind the chassis's front). 1.0: home (within 0.7 mm along the bay, so its connector is fully mated; within 1.5 mm across it; square within 2 degrees), its handle shut (within 3 degrees) under its catch (the catch dropped back within 0.5 mm of rest), no part of either gripper within 1 cm of the carrier, the carrier and handle still, for 1 s. 0.5: home, the handle not locked (or a hand on it, or not yet still). 0.25: in the bay with its connector on the backplane's blade, not home. 0: anything else (for example short of the connector, or out of the bay).
reset_notes: Press the carrier's blue release button so the handle springs open, pull the carrier out by its handle, and lay it back at the marked spot on the table, front towards the robot, handle open. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: All contact and forces, no rules. The bay is a cage of collision boxes with lead-ins (0.5 mm play a side). The connector is two sprung contact shoes (6 N preload, 5000 N/m) that the backplane's tapered 2.4 mm blade spreads: up to 13 N to mate, 6.3 N to hold, within SFF-8482. The handle is hinged with an opening spring; its hook bears on the frame post's lip and cams the carrier 6 mm in. Its catch is a sprung tab. Inner shapes, springs and frictions are our estimates. Boxes.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right hand reaches down by the carrier and hovers there but never picks it up); demo: 1.0 (success at step 719)
